before: require "minitest/autorun" loads the installed Minitest 6 test library and runs discovered tests when the process exits. A subclass of Minitest::Test exposes test_ methods. Integer#clamp returns a value capped at its inclusive lower and upper bounds. assert_equal(expected, actual) checks a value; a failed assertion makes the test command fail.

The local command is ruby main.rb --verbose. Inspect the named test and assertion count, not just the process launching. Runtime durations and random seeds vary; the evidence checks stable result markers instead of pretending those details are fixed.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
require "minitest/autorun"
class ClampTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_upper
    assert_equal 10, 11.clamp(0, 10)
  end
end

```
Expected output or behavior: One named test and one assertion pass.. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
